title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: The StoryHearth home page offers a free digital preview and printed hardcover storybooks, with buttons to proceed, view pricing, or log in. It explains a three-step process: add family members, share a memory, then receive an illustrated story.
output.think_aloud: This sounds very relevant to me, and I can see that I would not need to pay for a digital preview. However, that first description is full of words I do not understand—“multimodal,” “generative narrative engine,” “artefacts,” and “corpus.” I would like the simpler explanation underneath to come first.

site_model.who_it_is_for: Families who want to preserve a personal memory as a story starring their relatives.

site_model.fit_for_me: It appears well suited to preserving a family story for Oliver, although I would need plain language and clear costs before trusting it with personal details.

page_review.purpose: Introduce the personalised storybook service and lead the visitor into creating a book, checking prices, or logging in.
page_review.what_is_happening: The home page displays the service proposition, prominent calls to action, a three-step explanation, customer quotations, and links to help, privacy, terms, and contact details.
page_review.first_impression: The warm cream colour and simple layout feel suitable for a family keepsake, but the opening description sounds technical and off-putting. The more straightforward “How it works” section reassures me.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes. I understand that “Proceed” should lead to creating a story, and the free preview means I can explore without paying.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes. The orange “Proceed →” button and “See pricing” button are both prominent.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Mostly. “Proceed” is clear enough, although “Create my storybook” would tell me more precisely where I am going. “See pricing” also matches what I want to know.

issues.title: The opening description uses unnecessary technical language
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Several of these words are unfamiliar, and they make a simple family activity sound complicated and artificial.
issues.fix: Replace this with plain language such as: “Turn a treasured family memory into a personal storybook starring your loved ones.”

issues.title: Exact hardcover prices are not shown on the landing page
issues.evidence: The page says “See pricing” and “Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK” but gives no price.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to understand the cost before becoming committed, although the separate Pricing link makes it reasonable to check.
issues.fix: Show a clear starting price, such as “Hardcovers from £24.99,” while retaining the Pricing link.

issues.title: The decorative image has no description
issues.evidence: The image beside the opening text is shown as “image (no description)”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A meaningful description would make the example understandable if I were using a screen reader or could not see the image.
issues.fix: Add concise alternative text describing the personalised children's book and family characters.
